paper_title: Axion-like Relics: New Constraints from Old Comagnetometer Data
notes: Paper (Bloch, Hochberg, Kuflik, Volansky, arXiv:1907.03767) recasts old K-3He comagnetometer data (Vasilakis 2009, Kornack, Brown 2011) into new 95% CL limits on ALP-neutron coupling gaNN over ma < 4e-13 eV (extending to arbitrarily low masses), plus weaker ALP-electron limits (Fig. 4, not extracted here). The paper's exclusion curves are given only in Figures 3-4 with no numerical table; data_points are approximate reconstructions anchored by explicit text values: constant-field bound |b_n| < 5.5e-33 GeV (95% CL) for ma < 1.8e-22 eV with rho_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 and v ~ 7.7e-4 gives naive gaNN ~ 3e-9 GeV^-1, weakened by the stochastic-field correction. Coupling type is unambiguous (primary result is neutron coupling) but numerical values carry O(few) uncertainty. Paper also contains sensitivity projections (dashed curves) for future dedicated comagnetometer runs, not included in data_points. To convert emitted gaNN [GeV^-1] to dimensionless g_an multiply by 2*m_n ~ 1.88 GeV. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('union of') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.6, 44)) | declaration reconciled to axis read-back: 'coupling squared, g^2 (axis read-back)' (model declared 'g_ann in gev^-1 as plotted on the y-axis of fig. 3 (alp-neutron derivative coupling, not dimensionless g_an)' — axis unit wins, #594 contract) | Vision: Traced lower envelope of the union of blue 'This work [I]/[II]/[III]' 95% C.L. regions in FIG. 3 (fig_02.png). Dataset III gives a plateau ~2-7e-7 GeV^-1 below 3e-18 eV, with a step near m_a=1.8e-22 eV (constant-field bound from 270-day exposure, stronger at ultra-light masses) and a narrow spike near 5e-20 eV. Dataset II bridges 3e-18 to 4e-17 eV; dataset I provides the deep minimum ~4e-10 GeV^-1 near m_a~1-3e-15 eV; dataset II again covers 2e-13 to 4e-13 eV where the bound terminates. The boundary is highly jagged (noise spectrum), so intermediate spikes are smoothed; values good to factor ~2. Y-axis is g_aNN in GeV^-1, emitted as plotted per contract (hint asked for dimensionless g_an; no conversion applied).
